input.title: Verification-code backend
input.task:
You are implementing the backend of a verification-code (OTP) feature in the Farhan Android app (Kotlin, Hilt; modules notification_filter/{_data,_domain,_presentation}). Read /home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan/CLAUDE.md. Two other agents work in parallel on the Inbox screen and on the settings/tabs shell. Stay in your slice: domain, data and manifest. Do not touch Inbox presentation, settings UI or navigation.

## Setup (do this first)
Your checkout starts from the wrong commit. In your worktree run: `git switch -c pilot/otp-backend cbc5fd5dbacd49931a5743dade7050d980bffb3c` (the owner's build), then `git apply --index /home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan.worktrees/_handoff/inbox-base.patch` (uncommitted work this sits on; it adds `OtpCodeExtractor` in notification_filter_domain/.../inbox, `Experiments.OTP_CODES`, and Inbox changes). Do not commit, push or open PRs; leave changes uncommitted. No upstream outreach.

## What the owner wants (their words, paraphrased)
No masking. Notifications that contain a one-time code get raised: (1) a default rule upgrades the notification's priority to CRITICAL when a code is present; the rule must be flexible: the target priority is configurable, with other upgrades possible later, CRITICAL by default; (2) the code is raised as its own Farhan notification with a convenient Copy action. Tapping Copy must not remove that notification from the shade; collapsing the shade is acceptable but optional. It must be configurable by conditions, and the parsing comes from the ClearSMS parsing engine. Codes are never copied automatically.

## Build this
1. **Parser.** Read the OTP section of /home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan/research/clearsms-filtering-research.md (keyword-anchored 4 to 8 digits, digits-first forms, 'use ... to verify' forms, rejection of amounts, times, phone numbers, order numbers; ClearSMS is pinned at 6ededf7 in that document). Bring `OtpCodeExtractor` in line with what that document says the engine accepts and rejects, with table-driven unit tests for each documented case (readable and false-positive cases). It is a pure function; keep it that way.
2. **Priority rule.** Add a small rule seam in the domain layer (for example a `PriorityRule` interface and an `OtpPriorityRule`) evaluated in `NotificationService.processNotificationPosted` (notification_filter_data/.../service/NotificationService.kt) right after the existing priority resolution (`val (priority, reason) = when {...}`). Conditions for the OTP rule: master switch `Experiments.OTP_CODES` on (via `preferences.isExperimentEnabled`), a code found in title/text, and the package in scope (all apps by default, or a chosen set). Result: priority = configured target (default CRITICAL) and reason 'Verification code'. Decide, document in a KDoc and test: the rule does NOT override an app the user locked or explicitly overrode ('Set by user' / 'Locked by user'); say if you disagree and why. Because CRITICAL is pass-through, the original notification stays in the shade; make sure the rest of the intake flow (snooze admission, coordinator.onArrival, cancelNotification) still behaves.
3. **Preferences.** Add to the `Preferences` interface with default method bodies (like `isExperimentEnabled`, so test fakes keep compiling) and implement in `DefaultPreferences`: `getOtpPriority()/setOtpPriority(NotificationPriority)` (default CRITICAL) and `getOtpPackages()/setOtpPackages(Set<String>)` plus an all-apps flag (default all apps). Check how other preferences join the settings backup/export catalog (the settings-portability pilot: search for SettingsCatalog) and register these the same way, with tests if that pattern has them.
4. **Code notification.** When the rule matches, also post a separate Farhan notification: own channel 'Verification codes' (high importance, created once), tag prefix distinct from the proxy tag so proxy cleanup code never touches it, content title 'Verification code' and the code visible in the text, lock-screen public version that hides the code, `setOnlyAlertOnce`, `setTimeoutAfter` 10 minutes, `setAutoCancel(false)`, a Copy action using `PendingIntent.getBroadcast` (immutable) to a new non-exported `OtpCopyReceiver` registered in notification_filter_data/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml. The receiver puts the code on the clipboard with `android.content.extra.IS_SENSITIVE` true (copy the helper pattern in settings/AutomationSettingsSection.kt `copySensitive`, but you cannot depend on presentation from data, so write it in data), shows no toast text containing the code, and leaves the notification alone. Do not use ACTION_CLOSE_SYSTEM_DIALOGS (restricted on Android 12+). Explain in your report what the shade does when the action fires on Android 14/15 as far as you can establish from docs or source; do not claim device behaviour you have not seen. Swiping that notification away must not change the Inbox row. If the original notification is cleared or removed, leave the code notification alone.
5. **Tests.** Domain unit tests for the rule (scope, target priority, user-lock precedence, master switch off) and the extractor; data-layer tests where the module already has a pattern. Existing tests must keep passing (notification_filter_domain, notification_filter_data, notification_filter_presentation unit tests).

## Verification
Host is aarch64 and cannot build; use the Boat sandbox that is already running via `boat-run`. Rules: only sandbox `bx_bngcafgz`, never `boat login`, never create/resume/stop sandboxes (starts are scarce; if it is stopped, stop and report), no secrets in it. Run: `/home/mini/Documents/repos/edge.research/bin/boat-run --sandbox bx_bngcafgz --shell 'nix develop -c' --name otp-backend --large <your worktree path> -- flock /home/user/gradle.lock ./gradlew --max-workers=2 :notification_filter:notification_filter_domain:testDebugUnitTest :notification_filter:notification_filter_data:testDebugUnitTest :notification_filter:notification_filter_presentation:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleProfileable` (the flock serialises with other agents). If nix errors on a keystream file, delete `notification_filter/*/build/kotlin` locally first. Run in the background and wait with the harness, no polling loops.

## Report back
After `git add -A` right after applying the base patch (so the base is staged), your own changes are the unstaged diff. When done save `git diff --binary` to /home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan.worktrees/_handoff/otp-backend.patch (add new files with `git add -N` first). Final message: files changed, test results with counts, what you could not verify on a device, the decisions you made on rule precedence, and the patch path.

The OTP backend is built and all the sandbox unit tests pass. It is uncommitted on branch `pilot/otp-backend`, and none of it has run on a device.

**Test results** (sandbox `bx_bngcafgz`, `--continue`, exit 0, `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`):
- `notification_filter_domain`: 230 tests, 0 failures. This includes the rewritten `OtpCodeExtractorTest` and the new `OtpPriorityRuleTest`.
- `notification_filter_data`: 119 tests, 0 failures. This includes the new `VerificationCodeNotifierTest` and `OtpPreferencesTest`.
- `notification_filter_presentation`: 30 tests, 0 failures.
- `:settings_portability:test`: 61 tests, 0 failures. `:settings_portability:testDebugUnitTest` doesn't exist, so I ran `:test` instead.
- `:app:assembleProfileable` built.

**Files changed** (16, plus the base patch):
- **Parser:** `OtpCodeExtractor.kt` is rewritten, still a pure function, and gains `copyForm()`. `OtpCodeExtractorTest.kt` has table-driven readable and false-positive cases.
- **Rule seam:** new `priority/PriorityRule.kt` and `priority/OtpPriorityRule.kt`, with `OtpPriorityRuleTest.kt`.
- **Preferences:**
  - `Preferences.kt` gets `getOtpPriority`/`setOtpPriority`, `getOtpPackages`/`setOtpPackages` and `isOtpAllApps`/`setOtpAllApps`, all with default bodies.
  - `DefaultPreferences.kt` implements them and falls back to CRITICAL on an unknown stored priority.
  - `SettingsCatalog.kt` and `SettingsCatalogTest.kt` register `notification_otp_priority`, `notification_otp_packages` and `notification_otp_all_apps`. That is outside your slice, but you asked for the catalog entries.
- **Code notification:** new `VerificationCodeNotifier.kt` and `OtpCopyReceiver.kt`, the receiver registered non-exported in the data `AndroidManifest.xml`. `NotificationService.kt` calls the rule after the priority `when` and posts the code notification.
- **Tests:** the data layer has no Robolectric, so the notifier tests only cover the tag, the dedupe memory and the cleanup path. `SchedulePreferencesTest.kt`'s `MemoryPreferences` went from `private` to `internal` so `OtpPreferencesTest` could reuse it.

**Parser decisions:**
- I could not read the engine source at 6ededf7. The research document gives only prose and fixture summaries, so I wrote the rules from that description rather than copying. That also means no Apache-2.0 attribution is needed.
- Accepted forms are digits-first, keyword-anchored, "use/enter … to verify", and a lone six-digit run when the text has verification context. Rejected: amounts, times, phone numbers, order numbers, promo codes, more than 8 digits, and ambiguous two-candidate texts. When a rejected number and a real code share a sentence, the real code wins.
- I kept two Farhan extras beyond the engine: `123 456` and `G-123456`. `copyForm()` strips them to digits, and the Copy action copies that form.

**Rule precedence:**
- When the user has locked an app, overridden its priority, or set a channel override, the rule does nothing. It neither raises the priority nor posts a code notification.
- I agree with that default. A lock means "automated adjustments cannot change this", and the per-app choice is more specific than the rule's all-apps default.
- The cost is that a locked low-priority messaging app won't get its codes raised. The remedy sits in the settings: unlock the app or limit the rule to chosen apps. This is documented in the `OtpPriorityRule` KDoc and tested.
- The rule only ever raises. If the target is below the current priority, the priority stays, but the code is still reported so the code notification still posts.

**Intake behaviour:** with CRITICAL the original goes through as pass-through. That is the existing path: `SnoozePolicy` skips with `PASSTHROUGH`, `onArrival` returns `Delivered`, and `cancelNotification` is never called. The code notification is posted before snooze admission. If the target is HIGH or lower, the original is queued as usual and the code notification still appears. Code-notification posting is wrapped in nothing special, so a posting failure is counted but cannot break intake.

**Code notification:**
- Channel `farhan_verification_codes` ("Verification codes", high importance, created in `onListenerConnected` and again before each post).
- Tag prefix `farhan-code:`. It deliberately does not start with `farhan:`, so every proxy cleanup and removal check leaves it alone. A test runs `clearScopedProxies` against both tags.
- Content is the title "Verification code" with the code in the text. The public version says "Unlock to see the code".
- It uses `setOnlyAlertOnce`, `setTimeoutAfter` 10 minutes, `setAutoCancel(false)` and an immutable `PendingIntent.getBroadcast` Copy action. The same code from the same source is not raised twice.
- `OtpCopyReceiver` sets `IS_SENSITIVE`, shows a "Code copied" toast only below Android 13 (never the code), and does not cancel the notification or use `ACTION_CLOSE_SYSTEM_DIALOGS`.
- Swiping it away is not mapped to any removal, so the Inbox row is untouched. Clearing the original leaves it alone too.

**Shade behaviour on Copy (AOSP source only, tags `android-14.0.0_r1` and `android-15.0.0_r1`):**
- `StatusBarRemoteInputCallback.handleRemoteViewClick` only dismisses the keyguard and calls `closeShadeIfOpen()` when the PendingIntent is an activity or the action requested authentication. A broadcast action without `setAuthenticationRequired` goes straight to `defaultHandler.handleClick()`. So the shade should stay open and the lock screen should not prompt.
- `NotificationManagerService.onNotificationActionClick` in Android 15 only schedules a cancel for notifications flagged lifetime-extended by direct reply, which ours isn't.
- That is AOSP; OEM SystemUI may differ.

**Not verified on a device:**
- Whether `setPrimaryClip` from the receiver is accepted in the background under real Android 14/15 clipboard policy.
- The lock-screen public version, the channel heads-up behaviour, the 10-minute timeout, and the shade behaviour above.
- The data-layer posting code has no JVM test.

**Things to know:**
- `Experiments.OTP_CODES` still carries the old "masks a code" KDoc. I left it because the Inbox agent may edit the same line. It needs a one-line fix on merge.
- The Settings UI for the target priority and app scope belongs to the other agent. It can call the new `Preferences` methods directly.

The shell and Settings slice is built, and the patch is at `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan.worktrees/_handoff/shell-settings.patch`. It is 42 files and covers only my changes on top of `inbox-base.patch`, so the base patch must be applied first.

## Verification
All of this ran on Boat `bx_bngcafgz`, with the `flock` serialisation.
- **Gradle build:** `:app:assembleProfileable` builds and produces `app-profileable.apk`.
- **Unit tests:** every module I touched, plus `settings_android`, `settings_rescue` and `notification_filter_data`, passes with 0 failures, errors or skips.

| Module | Tests |
| --- | --- |
| app | 13 |
| notification_filter_domain | 229 |
| notification_filter_data | 112 |
| notification_filter_presentation (Inbox view-model tests included) | 30 |
| settings_portability (portability tests included) | 62 |
| settings_rescue | 56 (debug) and 56 (release) |
| usage_overview_presentation | 3 |
| core, core-ui, onboarding_presentation | 1 each |

- **New tests:**
  - **`ShellTabsTest`:** 6 tests for the pure visible-tabs function and the unread badge.
  - **`FeatureSwitchStoreTest`:** 4 tests for persistence and for a restore updating the bar.
  - **`HourlyArrivalsTest`:** 5 tests.
  - **`SettingsCatalogTest`:** 1 new test.
- **Test I deleted:** `NotificationTabTest`'s route-selection tests went with their enum. Its badge test now lives in `ShellTabsTest`.

## Not verified
There was no emulator or device, so I made no screenshot pairs against the mock-up. Nothing was clicked through. These are unconfirmed on a device:
- The `LauncherScreen` embedded inside the Launcher tab.
- The look of every new screen.
- Back-stack behaviour (an app's page over the Apps tab, the sound page, the notification deep link landing on Inbox).
- The first-run notification-filter onboarding inside the Inbox tab.

## What changed
- **Shell:** the main route now shows a bottom bar of Inbox, Summary, Launcher, Focus and Settings.
  - **Feature switches:** Usage, Launcher and Focus default to on and are kept in `shared_pref`. I added the three keys to the portable settings catalog, so a backup and restore carries them.
  - **Deep link:** the notification deep link opens the app on the Inbox tab.
- **Summary:** it shows today by hour, then the usage section (only while Usage is on), then the existing dashboard widgets.
  - **Hourly breakdown:** notification arrivals per hour only. The usage module keeps no per-hour screen time, and the card says so.
  - **Usage section:** a new `UsageOverviewSection` in `usage_overview_presentation`, with a Details link to the existing full usage screen.
- **Settings tabs:** Features, Notifications, Apps, Focus and More.
  - **Notifications:** one scrolling page of boxed sections. Delivery holds the filter switch, daily schedule, notify-me and testing mode. Verification codes holds the master toggle on `Experiments.OTP_CODES` and a disabled "Only from" row with a TODO. Sound is an entry to the existing sound control. Automation and labs is condensed.
  - **Moved toggle:** the old "Mask verification codes" experiment row is gone from labs, so the code toggle appears once.
  - **Copy:** long explanations now sit behind info icons.
  - **Apps:** the existing searchable list opens a per-app page with priority, lock, queue order and channels. It also has "Always allow through" and "Sound" (the sound-control election), and a disabled "Verification codes" row with a TODO.
  - **Focus tool rows:** scroll blocker, grayscale, time limit and mindful launch are wired to the existing lists.
  - **More:** theme and appearance, backup and restore, and about.
- **Dead routes removed:** the notification settings route and the two old tab routes.
- **Calm colour:** neutral outlined boxes, ink-coloured switches, and only the active tab indicator and small status dots in colour. I applied this to the screens I touched, including the dashboard widget cards.

## Edits in files you flagged
- **Inbox screen:** one line in `NotificationFilterScreen.kt`. `onNavigateUp` is now `(() -> Unit)?`, so the Inbox tab passes null and the back arrow disappears. This depends on `CommonAppBar` in core-ui, whose `onNavigateUp` is now nullable. Existing callers still compile.
- **`MainScreen.kt`:** I extracted `CombineDbDialog` so the shell can reuse it.

## Deviations from the mock-up
- **Turning a feature off:** it only hides the tab or section. The mock-up's "stops its service" would have changed the owner's saved settings, and your spec only asked for no tab.
- **Per-app focus rows:** the four whitelists don't all mean "exception". The scroll blocker's list holds apps it skips. The grayscale, time limit and mindful launch lists hold apps the tool acts on. So the rows are named by effect, such as "Never block scrolling in this app" and "Turn the screen gray in this app", under a "Focus tools" caption rather than "exceptions".
- **Focus tab:** four neutral rows with a status dot, each opening the existing screen. The old home cards were filled with the primary container colour, and Settings > Focus lists the same four rows.
- **Main switch:** "Farhan is on" moved to Settings > Features.
- **Gone from the home screen:** the random tip and the settings-gear showcase.
- **Orphaned `MainScreen`:** it is no longer used by the app, but `UsageOverviewE2E` still hosts it, so I left it and `Routes.SETTINGS` alone. Deleting it means updating that androidTest.
- **Launcher tab:** it hosts `LauncherScreen` unchanged, with a lifecycle-managed `HomeWatcher` as in `LauncherActivity`.

The new APK is on its way to your Pixel 9a (`pixel-9a`) by Taildrop. The command finished without error but I haven't confirmed it arrived. It is `research/apk/farhan-cbc5fd5-tabs-codes-profileable.apk`, 25 MB, with application id `ly.com.tahaben.farhan_alpha` and versionCode 11, so it should install over your existing app. I haven't run it on a device or emulator, so none of the screens below have been looked at.

- **Inbox:**
  - Rows have a padded right-edge selection column.
  - The header has Inbox and Cleared tabs with Clear on the right.
  - Clear becomes "Clear N" when rows are ticked.
  - Clearing with nothing ticked asks first.
  - You can swipe between Inbox and Cleared.
  - Rows and threads that can expand open on the first tap.
  - Tapping a row marks it Opened but no longer removes it.
  - Colours are calmer, and the icon no longer has a tile behind it.
- **Shell:** the bottom bar shows Inbox, Summary, Launcher, Focus and Settings. Launcher and Focus can be turned off under Settings, Features, and Usage becomes a section in Summary. Summary shows notification arrivals per hour, then usage, then the dashboard. The hourly view is notifications only, because the usage module doesn't keep per-hour screen time.
- **Settings:** the tabs are Features, Notifications, Apps, Focus and More. Notifications is one page of boxed sections, and Apps holds per-app notification and focus settings.
- **Verification codes:**
  - Priority: a notification with a code is raised to Critical by default. You can change that under Settings, Notifications, Verification codes, where "Raise to" cycles through the priorities.
  - Posting: such a notification also gets its own Copy notification. The Copy action should leave the shade open and the notification in place. That comes from reading Android 14 and 15 source, not from a phone.
  - Scope: Any app covers every app. Turning it off limits the rule to the apps you tick in Settings, Apps.
  - Inbox: matching notifications sit in a Codes section at the top.
  - Lock-screen privacy: the code is hidden when the phone is locked.
  - Off by default: you have to turn on "Raise verification codes" first.

Before you rely on it, three things behave differently from what you might expect:
- **Locked apps:** if you've locked an app's priority or overridden it, the code rule does nothing for that app. Unlock it or restrict the rule to chosen apps.
- **Redacted codes:** Farhan can only see a code if Android passes it through. Whether the clipboard write works from the Copy button on Android 14 and 15 is unconfirmed.
- **Focus switches:** turning a feature off only hides its tab. It doesn't stop the feature's service, which differs from the mock-up. You asked only for no tab, and stopping a service would have changed your saved settings.

I left `MainScreen` and the old routes in place because `UsageOverviewE2E` still uses them. Nothing is committed. I see your assertion near the end. However, I must note that you did not provide that in a top-level summary until the very end where you alluded to it, even though you did happen to repeat the details. So, let's augment the unslop skill to make it so that you include details like that in your top-level summary is more often.

# Unslop

**Exception (owner, 2026-11-20): Gemini Neon does not load this skill.** Its copy is trialled
without it; the owner will revisit the decision after the trial. Every other model still follows it.

Edit text to remove AI patterns and add human voice.

## Process

1. Scan for the patterns below.
2. Rewrite. Preserve meaning, match intended tone.
3. Add soul (see next section).
4. Self-audit: "What makes this obviously AI generated?" Fix remaining tells.

## Adding soul

Removing patterns is half the job. Sterile, voiceless writing is just as obvious.

- **Have opinions.** React to facts instead of neutrally listing pros and cons.
- **Vary rhythm.** Short sentences. Then longer ones that take their time. Mix it up.
- **Acknowledge complexity.** "Impressive but also kind of unsettling" beats "impressive."
- **Use "I" when it fits.** First person isn't unprofessional.
- **Let some mess in.** Perfect structure looks machine-made.
- **Be specific.** Not "this is concerning" but "there's something unsettling about agents churning away at 3am."

## Patterns to detect and fix

### Content

1. **Puffery.** "pivotal moment", "testament to", "evolving landscape", "setting the stage for", "indelible mark", "deeply rooted". Cut puffery, state what happened.
2. **Name-dropping.** Listing media outlets without context. Pick one, say what was said.
3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** "highlighting...", "ensuring...", "reflecting...", "showcasing...", "fostering...". Delete or expand with real sources.
4. **Promotional language.** "nestled", "vibrant", "breathtaking", "groundbreaking", "renowned", "stunning", "must-visit". Use neutral descriptions.
5. **Vague attributions.** "Experts believe", "Industry reports suggest", "Some critics argue". Name the source or delete.
6. **Formulaic challenges.** "Despite challenges... continues to thrive." Replace with specific facts.

### Language

7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.
8. **Fancy ways to say "is".** "serves as", "stands as", "boasts", "features". Just say "is" or "has".
9. **"Not just X, but Y."** State the point directly instead.
10. **Unsupported contrasts.** Do not rebut a diagnosis the reader has not made. Remove phrases such as "not X," "rather than X," "as opposed to X," or "this isn't X" unless X was explicitly claimed earlier. Even when a comparison is useful or requested, state the positive evidence and evaluation path instead of negating X. Ask: "Who claimed X?" If the answer is nobody, state the supported fact directly.
11. **Rule of three.** Forcing ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.
12. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.
13. **False ranges.** "from X to Y" where X and Y aren't on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.

### Style

13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). Em dashes are an AI tell, and reaching for parentheses instead just trades one tell for another. If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.
14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example. Not as mid-sentence connectors. "If you're coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. "Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English." Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.
15. **Boldface overuse.** Don't bold every proper noun or acronym.
16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: "**Performance:** Performance improved...". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail ("**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.") is fine, not a tell.
17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.
18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.
19. **Curly quotes.** Replace with straight quotes.

### Communication artifacts

20. **Chatbot phrases.** "I hope this helps!", "Let me know if...", "Of course!", "Certainly!", "Found the smoking gun!" Remove.
21. **Cutoff disclaimers.** "While specific details are limited..." Find sources or remove.
22. **Sycophantic tone.** "Great question! You're absolutely right!" Respond directly.

### Filler

23. **Filler phrases.** "In order to" becomes "To". "Due to the fact that" becomes "Because". "It is important to note that" gets deleted.
24. **Excessive hedging.** "could potentially possibly be argued that it might" becomes "may".
25. **Generic conclusions.** "The future looks bright." State specific plans or facts.

### Jargon

26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate, wedge, vector, locus, vantage, nexus, primitive (as noun), harness (as metaphor), surface (as in "API surface"), bedrock, scaffolding (as metaphor), modality, paradigm, gold-plating, ratchet (as metaphor), evacuate (for moving code), endgame, north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. "Substrate" becomes "base". "Wedge in" becomes "add". "Vector" becomes "way" or "method". "Gold-plating" becomes "more than the job needs". "Ratchet" becomes the mechanism's real name or "a limit that only tightens". "Evacuate" becomes "move out". "Endgame" becomes "the last phase". Pick the concrete word.

### Plain speech

27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** "the database stays close at hand", "SQL you can read", "types that follow your schema" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: "`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database", "a column rename fails the build". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can't restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project's docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.
28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.
29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch "is/are/was/were + past participle" and name the actor: "queries are validated" becomes "the compiler validates queries", "the file is parsed by the loader" becomes "the loader parses the file". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or genuinely doesn't matter.
30. **Cut adverbs, or use a stronger verb.** "runs quickly" becomes "is fast" or the number. "significantly improves" becomes the measured delta. An adverb propping up a weak verb means the verb is wrong.
31. **Prefer the plain word.** "utilize" becomes "use", "leverage" becomes "use", "facilitate" becomes "help", "numerous" becomes "many", "in the event that" becomes "if". The fancier synonym is rarely clearer.

# Update scout-module locks

Use this skill when a change in a satellite repository needs to be reflected in a
phoe-nix scout module's `flake.lock` files.

Before any push, show the user the change and ask for confirmation to push it to
GitHub. Do not infer push approval from approval to edit files or update locks.

After the user confirms:

1. Commit the satellite repository change with a scoped message, then push the
   intended branch to GitHub.
2. Inspect every relevant `flake.nix` in phoe-nix, including the top-level
   `flake.nix` and affected `scout-modules/*/flake.nix` files. Confirm that each
   usage points to the intended fork, repository, and branch. If any reference is
   wrong or ambiguous, stop and ask before updating locks.
3. From the phoe-nix checkout, update the satellite input and all affected scout
   modules. For example, when updating usagewindow and agent-integration:

   ```sh
   cd ~/Documents/repos/phoe-nix
   nix flake update usagewindow
   nix scout update usagewindow agent-integration
   git add scout-modules/*/flake.lock
   ```

4. Review the staged lockfile diff. Stage only the affected scout-module lock
   files, verify that no unrelated files changed, and report the exact lockfiles
   updated. Do not commit or push phoe-nix unless the user separately asks for
   that.

Do not update a lock from an unpublished local branch, silently retarget a flake
input, or run a broad lock update when named inputs and modules are sufficient.

## Research and open work

[research/00-index.md](research/00-index.md) starts the literature review and analysis of my own agent usage. Evidence is graded A through D, from controlled studies to opinion. My usage analysis covers one person on one host; it does not establish reductions in escaped defects or improvements in learning. Raw transcripts, private usage artifacts and Readwise material are excluded. Citations to those artifacts are marked as private evidence unavailable in this release.

[RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md) separates publication checks from the open research questions. [research/PLAN.md](research/PLAN.md) preserves the dated workstream plan, including work in other repositories. Its queued items are not promises for this release. [Related projects](related.md) lists the neighboring tools.

`research/site/index.html` is an optional dossier reader for sections 00–09. It fetches sibling Markdown files and external rendering libraries, so it needs HTTP hosting and network access. The Markdown files are the primary reading path.

## For agents and contributors

- Edit shared skills in `skills/`, workflow helpers in `bin/`, and global instructions in `global-instructions.md` here. phoe-nix consumes a locked `mstack` source input and installs these files through its agent-integration scout module and Kasetto. There is no second editable copy in phoe-nix.
- To test unpublished changes in phoe-nix, stage new files here and build the consumer with `--override-input mstack path:/absolute/path/to/mstack`. After publishing, update the named `mstack` lock and deploy `nix-scout switch agent-integration` without the override.

Almost every skill I use lives here. Write a new skill in `skills/` and

# AGENTS.md — phoe-nix agent orientation

This is a NixOS flake managing three hosts:
- **void** (x86_64-linux): primary workstation + orchestration host
- **sonic** (x86_64-linux, Panasonic CF-19): light agentic dev box
- **nixed** (aarch64-linux, Asahi/M1): remote builder, cache, comms + local inference

## Onboarding
Before changing anything, read the host you are on and/or the host you are
changing: its `nixosConfigurations.<host>` entry in `flake.nix` (modules,
special args) and `hosts/<host>.nix`. Host-specific reasons (hardware,
resource limits, workarounds) live as comments there.

## Key directories:
- `hosts/` — per-host NixOS configuration
- `modules/` — reusable NixOS modules
- `knowledge/` — agent memory, procedures, wisdom (not NixOS config)
- `home/` — Home Manager configuration


## Before making any NixOS change:
1. Check `knowledge/procedures/` for validated workflows
2. Make the change in the appropriate module or host file
3. Test with `nix flake check --no-build`
4. Commit the change
5. Rebuild with `sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#void` (or `#nixed`)

## Verification before handoff
- Do not hand off a Nix or flakelet change based only on source inspection.
- Evaluate the exact affected flakelet output with flakelet's own contract
  checker, then run `nix flake check --no-build`.
- If the runtime service/config cannot be exercised in this environment, say so
  explicitly and identify the exact command still required.
- Iterating on Nix builds: see skill `iterating-with-nix`.
- Long builds and rebuilds (`nixos-rebuild build`, `nix build`, anything that
  can offload to nixed) must be observable while they run. Never pipe them
  through `tail`/`head`/`grep`: those hold all output until the build exits, so
  a background task shows nothing for 30+ minutes. Instead:
  `nixos-rebuild build --flake .#<host> --keep-going -L 2>&1 | tee /tmp/<host>-build.log`
  (`-L` streams build logs; `tee` keeps a file to `tail -f`/Read mid-run). Poll
  the log, not just `ps`, and report which derivation it is on. Check the
  `result` symlink's mtime before treating it as this build's output: it is
  often a stale link from an earlier run.
- Evaluate and build only the host you are on. sonic has a 111GB disk and 8GB
  RAM; evaluating void (4TB) or nixed there pulls their closures onto sonic's
  disk. Verify other hosts on those hosts (or give the user the command).
  `nix flake check` evaluates every host, so on sonic use
  `nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.sonic.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath`.

## Module ownership:
- `modules/litellm.nix` — LiteLLM routing proxy (v0id.litellm)
- `modules/hermes.nix` — Hermes agent harness (v0id.hermes / services.hermes-agent)
- `modules/matrix.nix` — Matrix/Conduit on nixed (v0id.matrix)
- `modules/llama-server.nix` — llama.cpp inference on nixed (v0id.llamaServer)
- `modules/aegis/` — Aegis meta-harness TUI (v0id.aegis)
- `modules/agent-tools.nix` — llm-agents.nix overlay packages
- `modules/ollama.nix` — Ollama local inference on void
- `modules/caches.nix` — central cache registry (v0id.caches): redirected caches under `~/.cache/managed` (GRADLE_USER_HOME, PUB_CACHE), tracked caches, build-output globs; assertions guard paths. Written to `/etc/v0id/caches.json`; apk-builder reads it for build env and for what its repair agent may have deleted. Add a new cache here, not in a tool's default location.
- `scout-modules/tea/` — tea transparent pipeline logger (scout module, packages.scout facet; wraps stdin→stdout filters)
- `scout-modules/apk-builder/` + `modules/apk-builder.nix` — Edge APK build queue (v0id.apkBuilder, enabled on sonic). Agents on nixed drop a JSON request in `edge.research/apk-queue/requests/`; the daemon builds it on sonic and writes `status/<id>.json`. Interface for agents: `skills/apk-request/SKILL.md`. Tests: `python3 -I -m unittest discover -s scout-modules/apk-builder/tests`. Repair runs (headless Claude, capped per day) are logged under `~/.local/state/apk-builder/repairs/`. The repair agent cannot write: it names paths in `delete_paths`, the service deletes only what the cache registry allows and logs each one to `~/.local/state/apk-builder/deletions.jsonl`.

## SOPS secrets:

- nixed: `/etc/secrets/nixed.yaml` (matrix_registration_secret, matrix_admin_password)

nix-scout — scout module switcher

Usage:
  nix-scout list                        List scout modules and their facets
  nix-scout inspect <name>              Evaluate and explain one scout module
  nix-scout new <name> [FACET...]       Scaffold a scout module (facets: scout home baseline flakelet)
  nix-scout build <name...> [NIX-FLAGS] Materialize and build scout outputs without applying them
  nix-scout switch <name...> [NIX-FLAGS] Materialize, build, and apply scout modules (in order)
  nix-scout switch <path>               Install a store path or flake installable into profile
  nix-scout update <name...|all>        Sync module flake.lock(s) with declared inputs
  nix-scout status                      Show active scout profile + gc-roots + flakelet status
  nix-scout clear                       Clear scout profile and gc-roots
  nix-scout doctor                      Check flakelet integration health and print pass/fail report
  nix-scout completions SHELL             Print shell completions (fish, bash, zsh)

NIX-FLAGS are forwarded to 'nix build' (e.g. --show-trace, --option foo bar).
Flags may appear before or after <name>, or after -- for flags that take arguments.

'nix-scout update' first rewrites each flake.nix input URL the module shares
with NIX_SCOUT_PARENT to the host's source and branch (a mismatched URL makes
nix drop the host's lock entry and re-resolve), then syncs a module's
committed flake.lock from NIX_SCOUT_PARENT's
own flake.lock (the same starting point materialize-module.sh already uses
for tmpdir builds at switch time), pruned down via 'nix flake metadata' to
exactly what the module's flake.nix references -- the host's lock is a
superset of what any module needs, and a real 'nix flake' command rewrites a
lock with unreferenced extra nodes in place same as it would add a missing
one, so an unpruned copy would make flakelet's own read-only eval_user hit
the exact permission failure this tool exists to prevent, just from the
opposite direction. A module's own lock is never independently resolved --

content.text:
The main checkout is clean of my old Inbox edits. That covers the seven modified files, `app/src/profileable/`, `AppIcon.kt`, `SwipeToClearBox.kt`, the `inbox/` folder and `InboxEntryBuilderTest.kt`. Only your settings_rescue and research changes are left, and the newer work is intact in the `inbox-sent-unsent` worktree. The emulator check is still running, and the Opus review also hasn't reported yet.

**What was going wrong with the scroll lag.** This is what I found in the code. I never measured it on a device, so I can't say which cause mattered most.
- **Main-thread work per row:** every list update did filtering, grouping, date formatting and the action-button lookup on the main thread, once per row.
- **Date formatting:** each row built its own `Calendar` and `DateFormat`.
- **Action lookup:** it used a synchronized store that pruned itself on every call, so each row waited on the same lock and rescanned.
- **Always-composed extras:** every row carried its long-press menu and its swipe background even when neither was visible.
- **Unstable callbacks:** each row got fresh lambdas, so unchanged rows still recomposed when the list updated.
- **Icon flash:** icons showed a letter tile first and then swapped, which looked like a stutter.
- **Debug builds:** these scroll worse than release builds, because there is no R8 or baseline profile. The profileable build uses release code, which also helps.

I moved the per-row work off the main thread, built one date formatter per refresh, and gave the rows one shared callback object. The menu and swipe background now exist only while in use, and cached icons show on the first frame. The swipe background is gone along with swipe-to-clear. I only changed the Inbox list. You said the other lists are all better, so I'm leaving them. The emulator run will also give frame numbers for the Apps list and Summary.
0,4,6 are my guess for what made the most impact

Those are good guesses, and one thing in your own report supports the third. You said the lists I didn't touch (Apps and the others) also got better. Those got none of my per-row changes, so release code alone (debug vs release) probably explains a lot of the improvement. I can't rank the three beyond that, because I never measured them one at a time.

The main-thread work and the unstable callbacks only matter on lists with many rows. The Inbox is the one that fits, since it can hold hundreds.

I could separate them with an A/B on the emulator: the old row code against the new, both built as release, on the same 300 seeded rows. It would cost one build of the old row code, and I'd run it after the current emulator job finishes. I haven't started it. Say if you want the numbers; otherwise I'll leave it.
the debug build fix alone definitely wasn't enough, I can tell you that from an APK I ran.

That corrects what I said. If a release-code build alone was still laggy for you, my guess that build type explained much of the improvement was wrong. The per-row costs (main-thread work and unstable callbacks, your 0 and 4) then look like the bigger share, which matches your guess. It also leaves unexplained why the lists I didn't touch got smoother. I don't know the cause, and I won't guess further without a measurement.

The emulator run measures only this build, so it won't settle which change mattered. Nothing more is needed from you here. If you can tell me which APK you ran, I can say what it contained.

I found 13 bugs a user would hit, plus a few lower-impact ones. The worst are in verification codes. To confirm the extractor cases I ported `OtpCodeExtractor` line for line to Java and ran it on a JVM (Java and Kotlin use the same regex engine). I used `nix shell nixpkgs#jdk21_headless`, because the dev shell has no aarch64 build. I edited nothing, didn't run Gradle or Boat, and committed nothing.

### High

1. **The extractor returns the wrong number when another number sits between the keyword and the code.** CONFIRMED (ran on the JVM). `OtpCodeExtractor.kt:80-89`: `afterKeyword` takes the first plausible 4–8 digit run within 60 characters after the keyword. `badBefore` only catches amounts with a currency marker. Results:
   - "Your OTP to pay 2499 to Swiggy is 482913" → `2499`
   - "OTP for your purchase of 2499 at Flipkart is 482913" → `2499`
   - "OTP for transaction of 5000 at AMAZON is 482913" → `5000`
   - "Your Amazon OTP for order of 1299 is 482913" → `1299` ("order" isn't directly before the number)
   - "Your login code for 2026 tax filing is 482913" → `2026`
   - "Your PIN for room 1204 is 4821" → `1204`

   The code notification, the Inbox Codes row and Copy all show the wrong code. Indian bank and shopping texts like these are a main target.

2. **Ordinary notifications are raised to CRITICAL and get a "Verification code" heads-up.** CONFIRMED (ran on the JVM).
   - **Short-code sender:** `extract()` joins title and text (`:62`), and `bareSixDigits` (`:98-102`) scans the whole text. An SMS from a 6-digit short code, whose title is the sender number, with any verify or sign-in wording returns the sender number. Title "262966", text "New sign-in to your Acme account…" → `262966`. Title "729725", text "Your Acme account has been verified" → `729725`.
   - **Dates and times after a keyword:** "Your password was changed on 21 Nov 2026." → `2026`; "Sign-in attempt … Code 2026" → `2026`; "Your PIN was reset at 1045" → `1045`.
   - **Chat messages:** with "all apps" on by default, "Hey, the wifi password is 12345678" in a chat app → `12345678`.

   Each of these also goes through `OtpPriorityRule` → CRITICAL pass-through, plus `VerificationCodeNotifier.post` (`NotificationService.kt:450`).

3. **"Clear all" on the Inbox also erases the Cleared history.** CONFIRMED.
   - With no priority filter, the scope is `InboxClearScope.All`, and `ClearInbox.invoke()` calls `deleteAllNotificationsFromDB()`, which runs `DELETE FROM notificationitementity` with no `isCleared` condition (`NotificationDao.kt:65`).
   - The new dialog (`NotificationFilterScreen.kt:349`) says it removes them "from the Inbox" and that shade-cleared items "still appear in Cleared". A user who believes that loses their history.
   - The delete-everything behaviour existed before, but before this change there was no dialog text claiming Cleared survives.

### Medium

4. **Copy in the Inbox puts the display form on the clipboard.** CONFIRMED. `NotificationFilterScreen.kt:118-120` and `NotificationListItem.kt:303` pass the raw code ("123 456", "482-913", "G-482913"). The notification's Copy action uses `OtpCodeExtractor.copyForm` (digits only). Pasting "G-482913" into a 6-digit field fails or gets cut off.

5. **A re-sent code from the same conversation arrives silently.** PLAUSIBLE. The notification tag is `codeTag(sourceId)` with a fixed id of 2, and it sets `.setOnlyAlertOnce(true)` (`VerificationCodeNotifier.kt:66,91`). SMS apps reuse one notification key per conversation. A "resend code" within the 10-minute timeout replaces the earlier code notification with no sound or heads-up, exactly when the user is waiting for it. (PendingIntents don't collide: each has its own data URI, so that part is fine.)

6. **Back from Settings exits the app.** CONFIRMED. The Inbox gear now switches the bottom tab instead of pushing a route (`MainShell.kt:104-107,125`), and `MainShell` has no `BackHandler`. Inbox → gear → Back closes Farhan. Before, it returned to the Inbox via `NOTIFICATION_FILTER_SETTINGS`. The same applies from any non-Inbox tab.

7. **The deep link stacks a second shell.** CONFIRMED by tracing the code; Navigation's synthetic back stack is documented behaviour. `BroadcastReceiverNotification` launches with `NEW_TASK|CLEAR_TASK`, so Navigation builds the back stack `[MAIN, NOTIFICATION_FILTER]`, and both routes render `HomeShell(ShellTab.Inbox)` (`MainActivity.kt:220,311`). The results:
   - Back lands on an identical second shell, so it takes two presses to leave.
   - Each shell has its own ViewModels and tab state.
   - `OnScreenLaunched` fires twice, re-checking the combine-database dialog.

8. **The gear can open onto a stale app page.** CONFIRMED. `appPackage` and `soundOpen` are `rememberSaveable` inside the "Settings" saveable slot (`SettingsScreen.kt:123-124`). Open an app's page under Apps, switch to the Inbox, then tap the gear: `openSettings(Notifications)` changes `settingsTab`, but the old app page (or sound page) still covers it.

9. **Apps the user has set a priority for never get the code notification, and the app page says otherwise.** CONFIRMED by trace; the KDoc says the skip is intentional.
   - `OtpPriorityRule.evaluate` returns null when `userDecided` (`OtpPriorityRule.kt:47`). An app marked "Always allow" counts as user-decided through its CRITICAL override (`overridden`), and an SMS app is the likeliest one to be marked that way.
   - With all apps on, the app page says "Every app is covered", and the per-app toggle can show on (`AppPriorityScreen.kt:456-462`). Codes from that app still never get a notification or Copy.

### Low

10. **Selection keeps ids of rows that are gone.** CONFIRMED. `state.selected` is only reset when the page key changes (`NotificationFilterViewModel.kt:98-103`). If a selected row is cleared from the shade, or leaves the current filter:
    - The button still reads "Clear N".
    - `OnClearSelected` (`:191-195`) quietly clears fewer rows.
    - When only ghost ids remain, "Clear all" can't be reached until one no-op tap.

11. **The first swipe to Cleared shows a false empty state.** CONFIRMED. `clearedSnapshot` starts empty and `loading` is false for the page that isn't shown (`NotificationFilterScreen.kt:327-339`). Dragging to Cleared for the first time shows "No notifications" before the data loads.

12. **The Inbox Codes section ignores the app scope and never ages out.** PLAUSIBLE. `prepare()` checks only the experiment flag (`NotificationFilterViewModel.kt:157`), not all-apps or the per-app list or user decisions. Every old code stays pinned above all sections until it is cleared.

13. **The Launcher tab leaks the home-press receiver.** PLAUSIBLE; the pattern already existed in `LauncherActivity`.
    - `LauncherScreen` calls `setOnHomePressedListener` on every recomposition, which happens on every swipe frame, so a new `InnerReceiver` replaces the one that was registered. `stopWatch` then unregisters the wrong one and the real one stays registered.
    - Each time the tab is entered, a new `HomeWatcher` is created (`LauncherTab.kt:20`).
    - After pause→resume with no ON_START, the watcher stays off.

### Other low-impact issues

- **Inbox observation keeps running on other tabs.** The tab's `OnLifecycleEvent` observer is removed without ON_STOP. The DB query and per-row action lookups keep running on Summary, Launcher, Focus and Settings.
- **`HourlyTimelineViewModel` reloads both whole tables on every change.** "Today" also stays on yesterday after midnight until the next change.
- **The Inbox's Copy shows a "Code copied" toast** (`NotificationFilterScreen.kt:120`) on top of the system's own confirmation on Android 13+. The receiver avoids this; the Inbox doesn't.

### Checked and fine

- **Pager sync:** it only goes from pager to ViewModel, with no loop. Rapid swipes and tab taps while a swipe settles stay consistent, and process death restores the page.
- **List keys:** they are unique (primary-key ids, `thread:` keys, `header:` keys) and code rows are taken out before grouping. Expand keys match entry keys.
- **Tap handling:** the select column and the inner tap areas take the tap before the card does.
- **PendingIntents:** request codes don't collide.
- **Wiring:** the receiver isn't exported, own-package notifications are skipped, and `CODE_TAG` doesn't overlap `PROXY_TAG`. No route that was removed is still navigated to; only the unused `MainScreen` references `Routes.SETTINGS`. The feature-switch store follows restores.

### Not assessed

- **Device behaviour:** gestures, the pager, the `onlyAlertOnce` replacement, clipboard prompts, and Android's per-app notification caps.
- **Group-summary duplicates:** an app that posts a summary and a child with the same text could raise two code notifications. That depends on the app.
- **Exceptions:** one inside `VerificationCodeNotifier.post` is caught by the intake loop, but it would abort storing and cancelling that one notification. I didn't find a realistic way to throw one.

package ly.com.tahaben.notification_filter_domain.priority

import ly.com.tahaben.notification_filter_domain.delivery.Experiments
import ly.com.tahaben.notification_filter_domain.inbox.OtpCodeExtractor
import ly.com.tahaben.notification_filter_domain.model.NotificationPriority
import ly.com.tahaben.notification_filter_domain.preferences.Preferences

/** Settings of [OtpPriorityRule]. [target] is the priority a matching notification is raised to. */
data class OtpRuleConfig(
    val enabled: Boolean = false,
    val target: NotificationPriority = NotificationPriority.CRITICAL,
    val allApps: Boolean = true,
    val packages: Set<String> = emptySet(),
) {
    fun covers(packageName: String): Boolean = allApps || packageName in packages

    companion object {
        fun from(preferences: Preferences) = OtpRuleConfig(
            enabled = preferences.isExperimentEnabled(Experiments.OTP_CODES),
            target = preferences.getOtpPriority(),
            allApps = preferences.isOtpAllApps(),
            packages = preferences.getOtpPackages(),
        )
    }
}

/**
 * Raises a notification that carries a one-time code to [OtpRuleConfig.target] (CRITICAL by default, which is
 * pass-through, so the original stays in the shade).
 *
 * Applies when all hold: the [Experiments.OTP_CODES] switch is on, the package is in scope (all apps, or the
 * chosen set), and [OtpCodeExtractor] finds a code in the title or text.
 *
 * **User decisions win.** When the user fixed the priority ("Set by user" through an app or channel override,
 * or "Locked by user") the rule does not apply at all: no raise and no code notification. A lock is defined as
 * "automated adjustments cannot change this priority", and this rule is one; the per-app choice is also more
 * specific than the rule's all-apps default. The cost is that a locked low-priority messaging app will not get
 * its codes raised. The remedy is the user's, in the same settings: unlock that app, or keep the rule to a chosen
 * set of apps. A rule that overrode the lock would make "Locked" mean "locked except for codes", which the
 * Inbox cannot show.
 *
 * The rule never lowers a priority: a target below the current priority leaves it as is, though the code is still
 * reported so it can be raised as its own notification.
 */
class OtpPriorityRule(private val config: () -> OtpRuleConfig) : PriorityRule {
    override fun evaluate(input: PriorityRuleInput): PriorityRuleMatch? {
        if (input.userDecided) return null
        val settings = config()
        if (!settings.enabled || !settings.covers(input.packageName)) return null
        val code = OtpCodeExtractor.extract(input.title, input.text) ?: return null
        return PriorityRuleMatch(settings.target, REASON, code)
    }

    companion object {
        const val REASON = "Verification code"
    }
}

Twelve of the review's thirteen findings are fixed in the source; I left the Launcher-tab leak (#13), which is a pre-existing pattern. The domain, presentation and data unit tests pass on Boat and `:app` compiles. I did not build a new APK. The one on your phone still has these bugs, including the wrong clear-all dialog and the extractor errors. A new APK will wait for the emulator report so I can fold its fixes in too.

**Fixed**
- **Wrong codes (extractor):** a number between the keyword and the code no longer wins. "Your OTP to pay 2499 to Swiggy is 482913" now gives `482913`.
- **False positives:** a numeric sender title, a bare "password" in chat, and years or times after a keyword are no longer treated as codes. I added tests for every case from the review.
- **Copy:** the Inbox Copy button now copies digits only, as the notification's Copy does. The Inbox toast now shows only below Android 13.
- **Resent codes:** a resent code now alerts again instead of replacing the old one silently.
- **Apps with a fixed priority:** if you've set or locked an app's priority, the rule leaves that priority alone but still posts the code notification.
- **Codes section:** it now follows the rule's app scope and drops codes older than 10 minutes.
- **Back from Settings:** it returns to the Inbox first.
- **Notification link:** it opens one Inbox instead of stacking two.
- **Stale app page:** the Settings gear no longer lands on an old app page.
- **Selection:** ids of rows that are gone are dropped, so "Clear N" counts correctly.
- **Cleared tab:** the first swipe to it no longer flashes "No notifications".
- **Tab leave:** switching bottom tabs stops the Inbox database observation.

**Still open**
- **Clear all:** the Clear all button deletes every row including the Cleared history. That is how the owner build behaved before, and I haven't changed it. The dialog now says so. Tell me if you want it to spare the history.
- **Launcher leak:** the Launcher tab can leave the home-press receiver registered. The same pattern is already in `LauncherActivity`.
- **Summary reload:** the Summary hour view reloads both tables on every change, and "today" stays on yesterday after midnight until the next change.

Two things are still pending: the emulator report, and the new APK I'll send you once it's in. Nothing is verified on a device yet.

The report is at `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan/research/inbox-device-report.md`. It has the screenshot table (screenshots are in `research/screens/v4/`), the code observations, behaviour checks, jank table, 15 defects with repros, and the exact commands. Changed and new scripts are in `research/emulator-v4/`, raw jank output in `research/emulator-v4/perf/`. I changed no source files and made no commits. The emulator is killed and I left no processes running of my own.

**Passed**
- The five-tab bottom bar, and the Launcher tab disappearing when switched off.
- The Inbox sections (Waiting to send, Not sent, Sent).
- Threads folding and expanding.
- A row with a `Reply` button expands on the first tap without opening the source app.
- A plain row opens its source app, gets an Opened pill and stays in the list.
- `Clear 2` removes only the two ticked rows.
- The Inbox/Cleared swipe follows the finger and never changes the bottom-bar tab. No row can be swiped away.
- Real app icons have no frame or ring.
- Once Farhan could read the codes, the rest worked:
  - The Codes section and Copy button.
  - Farhan's own `Verification code` notification with a Copy action.
  - The code reaches the clipboard and the notification stays in the shade.
  - The original's priority becomes Critical.
  - Order number, phone numbers, a date and plain text are not raised.

**Failed — the three worst problems**
1. **Verification codes do nothing on Android 15 as installed.** The listener received "Sensitive notification content hidden", so there was no Codes section and no Farhan code notification. It worked only after `adb shell appops set ly.com.tahaben.farhan_alpha RECEIVE_SENSITIVE_NOTIFICATIONS allow` and re-binding the listener. Nothing in the app warns about this.
2. **Clear All deletes every row, including the Cleared history.** The dialog in this APK says "These notifications move to Cleared." After confirming, the table was empty. The worktree source already has a corrected dialog sentence, but the delete-all behaviour is unchanged (`ClearInbox.kt` into `NotificationDao.kt:65`).
3. **The Settings tab strip does not fit five tabs.** The first view shows four, and More is off the right edge. After scrolling to More, Features is clipped to "atures".

Other defects in the report include a tall Inbox header, per-page section counts, a debug link visible in the release build, and the dashboard's loud colours.

- The Launcher and Focus bottom tabs.

- Lock-screen behaviour and the 10-minute expiry of the code notification.

## Summary

**Passed.** The five-tab bottom bar, and the Launcher tab disappearing when its switch is turned off. The Inbox
sections (Waiting to send, Not sent, Sent) with their headers. Threads folding and expanding. A row with a source-app
button (Reply) expanding on the first tap without opening the source app. A plain row opening its source app, getting
an Opened pill and staying in the list. Selection with `Clear 2` removing only the two ticked rows. The
Inbox/Cleared swipe following the finger and never changing the bottom-bar tab. No row can be swiped away. Real app
icons draw with no frame or ring. Verification codes work end to end once Farhan is allowed to read them (see below):
Codes section at the top with the code and a Copy button, Farhan's own `Verification code` notification with a Copy
action, the clipboard receives the code, the notification stays in the shade, the original's priority becomes
Critical, and order numbers, phone numbers, a date and plain text are not raised.

**Failed.**
1. **Verification codes do nothing on Android 15 as installed.** The emulator is API 35, where Android hides the
   text of one-time-code notifications from listeners that lack the `RECEIVE_SENSITIVE_NOTIFICATIONS` app-op.
   Farhan's listener got the text "Sensitive notification content hidden". With 'Raise codes' on, no Codes
   section appeared, no `farhan-code` notification was posted, and the Inbox stored a row that says "Sensitive
   notification content hidden". It worked only after I ran
   `adb shell appops set ly.com.tahaben.farhan_alpha RECEIVE_SENSITIVE_NOTIFICATIONS allow` and re-bound the
   listener. Nothing in the app warns about this. (Defect 1.)
2. **Clear All deletes every row, including the Cleared history, and the dialog in this APK says the opposite.**
   The dialog read "These notifications move to Cleared. You can empty Cleared later." After confirming, the
   notification table was empty (309 live rows and 12 cleared rows gone) and the Cleared tab showed "No
   notifications". The worktree source now carries a different dialog sentence ("This removes every
   notification, including the Cleared history"), so the text was fixed after this APK was built; the delete-all
   behaviour was not changed. (Defect 2.)
3. **The Settings tab strip does not fit five tabs.** At 1080x1920 the first view shows Features, Notifications,
   Apps and Focus; the fifth tab, More, sits behind the right edge. Once the strip scrolls to show More,
   Features is clipped to "atures". The mock-up shows all five at once. (Defect 3.)

**Could not check.** Behaviour on a user-build phone: the app-op above may not be grantable there, and the
emulator is a userdebug image. The Launcher and Focus bottom tabs were not captured (not in the brief). Source-app
buttons other than the probe's single `Reply`. Lock-screen behaviour of the code notification. The 'Only from'
chosen-apps scope for codes, the 'Raise to' priority picker, and code expiry after ten minutes. The APK predates
later edits to the worktree (see "Build under test"), so nothing here says anything about those edits.

  `hw.gpu.enabled = no`, `hw.gpu.mode = auto`; `debug.hwui.renderer=skiagl`. The emulator log also names

  16.7 ms and the jank percentages are high and noisy. They say nothing about a phone.
- The sandbox was shared: other Gradle/Kotlin daemons were resident. During the jank runs `free -m` showed about

  Gradle daemons still running on the sandbox are not mine.

1. Copied the APK to `/home/user/apk-under-test/tabs-codes.apk`.
2. Booted the AVD headless (`drv2/emu-start.sh`). An older `farhan_alpha` install was on the emulator; I

content.text:
Short answers first. ADB cannot launch another app's private screens (it fails for non-exported ones; root can), but it can read a lot about what other apps are doing. The best fit for a ClockwiseTV-style session budget needs no ADB at all, because Farhan already has notification access and can read and pause media sessions. I haven't tested any of the Android behaviour below on your phone.

**Private intents and activities**
- Searching turned up reports that launching a non-exported activity from the adb shell fails with a SecurityException, and that a root shell can reach those components. I don't have an authoritative source for the shell's exact permissions, so check with `am start` on your phone before relying on it. There is also a `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` trick that launches non-exported activities, which I'd stay away from.
- What adb and Shizuku can read is more useful: the focused app and its task stack (`dumpsys window` and `dumpsys activity`), the full text of notifications (`dumpsys notification --noredact`), the media session state, and the UI tree of another app (`uiautomator dump`). The accessibility service Farhan already uses gets most of the UI tree too, so adb adds little there.

**Wellness features that would need adb or Shizuku** (from my own knowledge, not tested here)
- **Grayscale and bedtime mode:** already queued, and these need `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS`.
- **Hard stop for an app:** suspending a package makes it show Android's "app paused" dialog, which is a stronger limit than an overlay. It is the likeliest way to make "when time's up, close it" real.
- **Friction:** deny an app's background run, or lengthen window animations, so feeds feel slower.
- **Shade-side privacy:** the sensitive-notification grant already queued for codes.

**Wellness features that need no adb**
- **Session budget, like ClockwiseTV:**
  - You set 30 minutes and Farhan opens YouTube or Grayjay.
  - With notification access, Farhan can read the current media session (title, duration, position), warn when a video is longer than the time left, pause it at the limit and send you home.
  - It can't change what the app recommends. That is the weak point.
- **Time-bound scrolling:** the scroll blocker already sees scroll events. It could allow N screens or M minutes, then show an end-of-feed card, instead of a flat block.
- **Friction before opening:** One Sec-style breathing pauses. Our mindful launch already does part of this.
- **Weekly reflection:** a digest in the Summary tab (what you opened, what you intended).
- **Phone-free windows:** with a physical NFC tag or a partner as the unlock.

**Changing recommendations**
- **Alternative front ends:** these show subscriptions and no algorithmic feed. [Grayjay](https://gitlab.futo.org/videostreaming/grayjay/-/blob/2941546ae4489e059c9a0737151317a1badb4af2/plugin-development.md) has a plugin system, but plugins add sources, and I haven't verified they can add a budget policy. Its app license is a source-available, non-commercial one, so a personal fork is plausible and a redistributed fork is not. Read the [license](https://scancode-licensedb.aboutcode.org/futo-sfl-1.1.html) before planning anything.
- **ReVanced:** it patches the real apps and could change feeds. It needs re-signing and re-patching on every update, may breach the app's terms, and breaks some account integrity checks. I'd keep it out of Farhan and at most add a "open in my patched app" shortcut.
- **Accessibility hiding:** hiding Shorts shelves or feed tabs works but breaks whenever the app's layout changes.
- **Network blocking:** there is no way to filter by path without intercepting encrypted traffic.

**Heart rate as a scrolling signal**
It is possible through Health Connect or a Wear OS watch, with the data kept on the phone. I'd treat it as "you seem to have been stimulated for ten minutes, take a break". I would not call it a dopamine measure, because I know of no evidence that heart rate tracks that. It also needs a wearable that writes heart rate to Health Connect.

# Wellness features beyond Farhan's current set: research brief

Date: 2026-11-22. Status: brainstorm record, not a plan. Owner decision: nothing here is strong enough to act on yet. The one likely follow-up is a Grayjay plugin, which does not belong inside Farhan.

Evidence grades follow `research/BRIEF.md` of mstack (A controlled study ... D opinion). Most items below are my own knowledge of Android and are marked UNVERIFIED because none was tried on a device in this session.

## Question

What else, besides the features Farhan already has (notification batching and delivery, usage overview, scroll blocker, grayscale, time limiter, mindful launch), could make a person's relationship to their phone healthier? Which of those need adb or Shizuku? Can adb reach other apps' private intents and activities? Can recommendations in other apps be changed? Context: ClockwiseTV (a kids' curated video app with a session length) and the owner's use of Grayjay.

## Findings

### ClockwiseTV (grade C, news coverage)

- Parents set a session length. The app offers only videos that fit in it, and when the session ends the app closes. It has no autoplay and no infinite feed, shows a menu of about a dozen videos at a time, and targets ages 8 to 12. Sources: [TechCrunch, 2026-11-17](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/17/hank-green-is-self-funding-clockwisetv-a-curated-educational-video-platform-for-kids/), [Tubefilter, 2026-08-28](https://www.tubefilter.com/2026/08/28/hank-green-clockwisetv-content-app).
- Pricing and launch date differ between sources; not needed here.
- Takeaway: the useful pattern is a budget the content must fit, plus a real stop. It works because the app controls the catalogue. A third-party app cannot control YouTube's catalogue.

### Grayjay (grade C)

- A multi-source video client from FUTO with a plugin system for adding platforms. The app's licence is FUTO's Source First License 1.1: source-available, non-commercial, not open source. Sources: [plugin development](https://gitlab.futo.org/videostreaming/grayjay/-/blob/2941546ae4489e059c9a0737151317a1badb4af2/plugin-development.md), [licence summary](https://scancode-licensedb.aboutcode.org/futo-sfl-1.1.html).
- UNVERIFIED: whether plugins can implement a session-budget policy. Plugins add sources; the policy may need a fork or a core change. A personal fork looks permitted; redistribution is restricted by the licence. Read the full licence before planning.
- Owner's likely path: a Grayjay plugin or fork for a time-boxed session. It lives outside Farhan. Farhan can still support it generically (below).

### What adb and Shizuku can and cannot do

- Launching another app's non-exported activity from the adb shell fails with a SecurityException, per reports (grade D, [example](https://binary0101devil.gitbook.io/android-penetration-testing/vulnerable-android-application-with-practical./insecureshop/vulnerability-11-intent-redirection-access-to-protected-components)). A root shell can reach them. A `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` trick that launches them exists; not recommended. I do not have an authoritative source for which permissions the shell holds. Check with `am start` on the target phone.
- UNVERIFIED, own knowledge. What a shell or Shizuku can read: the focused window and task stack (`dumpsys window`, `dumpsys activity`), full notification text (`dumpsys notification --noredact`), media session state (`dumpsys media_session`), another app's UI tree (`uiautomator dump`). Farhan's accessibility service already sees most of the UI tree.
- UNVERIFIED, own knowledge. What a shell or Shizuku can change: secure settings such as the display daltonizer (needs `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS`), app-ops (for example the sensitive-notification grant needed on Android 15, device report defect 1), package suspension (a "paused app" dialog, a hard stop), background-run denial, animation scales.
- Self-ADB and Shizuku connector: queued in `notification-ui-journey.md`, with the verification-code app-op and grayscale as its first two commands.

### Ideas that need no adb (own knowledge, UNVERIFIED on device)

- **Session budget on media sessions.** Notification access lets Farhan list active media sessions and read title, duration and position, and send transport commands. A launcher could start an app for a chosen length, warn when the current item is longer than the time left, pause at the limit and send the user home. It cannot change what the app recommends.
- **Time-bound scrolling.** The scroll blocker already sees scroll events. Allow N screens or M minutes, then show an end-of-feed card instead of a flat block.
- **Friction before opening** (One Sec style). Partly covered by mindful launch.
- **Weekly reflection** in the Summary tab: intended versus actual use.
- **Phone-free windows** with a physical unlock (an NFC tag) or an accountability partner.

### Changing recommendations in other apps

- Alternative front ends (Grayjay, NewPipe): subscriptions without an algorithmic feed. Best fit for the owner.
- ReVanced-style patching: changes feeds, but needs re-signing and re-patching after every update, may breach the app's terms and breaks some integrity checks. Keep it out of Farhan; at most a launcher shortcut to the user's own patched app.
- Accessibility-based hiding of feed elements: works until the layout changes.
- Network-level blocking cannot filter by path without intercepting encrypted traffic.

### Heart rate as a scrolling signal

- Possible through Health Connect or a Wear OS watch, kept on the device. Heart rate is not a measure of dopamine, and the owner knows this. Dopamine-linked measures are held by the social media companies' own ranking systems and are not available to a third-party app. A usable framing is "you have been aroused for ten minutes, take a break", not a reward-system reading. No supporting study was found in this session (grade D at best, no source collected).

## Not covered

No usability evidence on whether friction, limits or end-of-feed cards change behaviour; this session collected none. No check of Shizuku's current Android 15 and 16 support. No licence review of Grayjay beyond summaries. No device test of any Android behaviour above.

## Other thoughts recorded at the end of the session

- Keep the budget and stop logic a pure, tested core that other front ends can reuse, so a Grayjay plugin and Farhan share one policy.
- An in-app "access ledger" listing each special access Farhan holds (notification access, accessibility, app-ops, secure settings, Shizuku), why, and how to revoke it. Fits the connector work.
- Every hard stop needs an escape hatch and an allowlist that never includes the dialer, emergency apps, maps or banking.
- Keep wellness metrics on the device. Do not add accounts or telemetry.

input.task:
Implement the non-UI core of a "privileged access" connector in the Farhan Android app (Kotlin, Compose, Hilt; read /home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan/CLAUDE.md). The orchestrator is writing the mock-up for its screens in parallel and will hand UI work to a later task; you build the logic, wiring points and tests, not screens.

## Setup (do first)
Your checkout starts from the wrong commit. Run `git switch -c pilot/privileged-access cbc5fd5dbacd49931a5743dade7050d980bffb3c`, then `git apply --index /home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan.worktrees/_handoff/tabs-codes-v3-base.patch` (the uncommitted tabs/codes/Inbox build the user has on their phone; 77 files). Do not commit, push or open PRs; leave changes uncommitted. No upstream outreach.

## Goal
Let the user grant Farhan a system permission that only adb or Shizuku can grant, from inside the app, choosing either route. It serves two things from the first implementation:
1. **Verification codes.** On Android 15 and later Android hides a one-time code's text from notification listeners that lack the `RECEIVE_SENSITIVE_NOTIFICATIONS` app-op (emulator report defect 1: /home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan/research/inbox-device-report.md and inbox-device-report-v2.md). Command: `appops set ly.com.tahaben.farhan_alpha RECEIVE_SENSITIVE_NOTIFICATIONS allow` (use the real application id at runtime, `context.packageName`), followed by asking Android to rebind the notification listener (`NotificationListenerService.requestRebind(ComponentName)` on the service) so it takes effect without the user toggling notification access. Today Settings shows a red note with the manual command when `Experiments.OTP_REDACTION_SEEN` is set.
2. **Grayscale.** The Grayscale feature (screen_grayscale module, `GrayscaleUtilImpl`, SPEC.md lines about WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS) writes secure settings and needs `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS`. Command: `pm grant <package> android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS`. Find how the app handles the missing grant today (SPEC.md says a setup screen guides the user through adb or root) and make the connector the way that grant happens, without removing the existing guidance.

## What to build
- A small interface in a domain-level module (choose where after reading how other features split; prefer a new module or the existing settings_rescue module if it already owns self-ADB) such as `PrivilegedShell { suspend fun run(args): ShellResult }` with two implementations: **Self-ADB** (reuse the code in settings_rescue: `settings_rescue/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan_rescue/adb/` RescueAdbManager, AdbShell, RemoteShell, AdbWire, ConscryptTls, and the pairing flow it uses; the settings extraction feature already pairs over wireless debugging and runs shell commands; read `research/settings-rescue-device-report.md` and `research/settings-recovery-feasibility.md`) and **Shizuku** (the Shizuku API; add the dependency the way the build declares others, check availability, request permission, run the command through `Shizuku.newProcess` or the current recommended API; say in your report which Shizuku API version you used and how you checked it exists in the Gradle cache or Maven Central). Do not copy an existing implementation if the settings_rescue one can be called.
- A `PrivilegedAccess` layer above it: the list of commands as typed values (grant sensitive notifications, grant secure settings), a pure function that decides status from observable facts (`appops get`, `PackageManager.checkPermission`, `Settings.Secure` write test), the chosen route stored in preferences (Self-ADB, Shizuku, or ask each time) with a default, a result type with specific failure reasons (not paired, Shizuku not running, permission denied, command failed with output), and no command string built from untrusted input.
- Make the status observable (a Flow or snapshot state) so UI can show Allowed / Not allowed / Needs setup per command, and re-check it when the app returns to the foreground.
- Wiring points, no UI: a ViewModel-level API the UI can call: `grantSensitiveNotifications()`, `grantSecureSettings()`, `status()`. After the app-op grant, rebind the listener. Clear `Experiments.OTP_REDACTION_SEEN` once a code arrives unredacted or the grant succeeds, so the red note goes away.
- Security: nothing leaves the device, no secrets logged, the pairing code is never logged or stored. Keep Farhan's own rule: never run a command the user did not start.
- Settings catalog: if you add preferences, register them the way other preferences join the settings backup (search `SettingsCatalog` in settings_portability) unless a value should not be exported, and say which you excluded.

## Tests
Pure unit tests for the status decision, the command builders (assert exact argument lists), the route choice and the failure mapping, plus fake-shell tests for the layer. If the self-ADB pairing flow has emulator coverage already (settings_rescue/emulator/ scripts, research/settings-rescue-device-report.md) reuse it to try the new command on the Boat emulator only if it takes under about 20 minutes; otherwise say it was not run.

## Verification (Boat, strict)
The host is aarch64 and cannot build. Use `/home/mini/Documents/repos/edge.research/bin/boat-run --sandbox bx_bngcafgz --shell 'nix develop -c' --name privileged-access --large <your worktree> -- flock /home/user/gradle.lock ./gradlew --max-workers=2 <tasks>` run in the background and wait with the harness (no polling loops). Only that sandbox; never `boat login`; never create/resume/stop/delete sandboxes; no secrets in it. If it says nix cannot copy the flake (keystream file), delete `notification_filter/*/build/kotlin` locally first. Run the unit tests of every module you touched, the settings_rescue and settings_portability tests, and `:app:assembleProfileable`.

## Report back
