Mostly yes, it's a one-time step, but I haven't tested any of this on your phone and there are caveats. I've updated the mock-up to v5 with your toggle and revoke rules, and passed the same rules to the connector delegate ([Privileged-access connector core](t3-thread://v2/11f16558-25cd-4565-8168-ccbffcb555b6/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3Afe47e575-aefc-4d1d-8295-7533fc077d00%3Adelegate-task%3A5a7f132c-a99f-48fd-947b-517b61d19d2f)).

**Is it one time?** Mostly yes. These points come from what I know of Android and are not verified on your phone:
- **The code can't be kept.** The pairing code works once. What Farhan can keep is the key it pairs with, so later grants and revokes need no code.
- **The grants should survive reboots.** Both the sensitive-notifications setting and the grayscale permission should persist until revoked or until Farhan is uninstalled. A reinstall over the existing app should keep them, but I'm not sure.
- **Each later toggle needs a live connection.** For wireless debugging that means the phone is on Wi-Fi with Wireless debugging switched on, and it can turn itself off when you change networks. Shizuku has to be running. If the connection is missing, the toggle fails and says why.
- **Possible hands-free toggles (guess).** Once Farhan holds the grayscale permission, it may be able to switch Wireless debugging on by itself for later toggles. I haven't confirmed that, so the build won't rely on it.
- **Revoking needs the connection too.** Farhan can't undo these grants by itself, so switching an access off also needs the connection.

**What changed in v5:**
- **After one Allow:** the other access becomes a plain switch, and the red note's Allow runs directly with no flow. A "Connected" row shows which route is kept (wireless debugging or Shizuku).
- **Both switched off:** the pairing is forgotten, so the next Allow pairs again.
- **New "Phone forgot Farhan" outcome:** if the phone no longer trusts Farhan, both accesses switch off and you're sent back to pairing.
- **Copy:** the flow now says the code works once, and Farhan keeps only the key.

The non-UI core of the privileged-access connector is built and builds green on Boat, but nothing in it has been run on a real device, and one decision needs the owner's call. Merging this adds the `INTERNET` permission to Farhan, which contradicts SPEC.md line 5 and onboarding page 1 ("no internet permission"). Android requires `INTERNET` for any socket, loopback included. I kept all of the Self-ADB route (and so the permission) in its own module, `:privileged_access:privileged_access_selfadb`. Dropping that dependency removes the permission, libadb, Conscrypt and Bouncy Castle, but the Hilt graph then needs a `SelfAdbRoute` binding that reports `ANDROID_TOO_OLD`; I did not write that fallback. The APK also grows by Conscrypt's native libraries, which I did not measure.

## Not verified on a device
- **Self-ADB on a retail Android 15 or 16 phone.** The emulator's adbd does not require authentication, so a secure adbd accepting Farhan's key is untested. The new route was not run on the Boat emulator: the helper's emulator scripts exist only in the main checkout's uncommitted tree and there is no UI to drive the new route.
- **mDNS port discovery** (`AdbDiscovery`, NsdManager) has never run anywhere. It follows how Shizuku finds the port.
- **Shizuku route.** Shizuku is not installed on any device I could use, and the user-service handoff has never run.
- **`pm revoke ... WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` may kill Farhan's process.** I could not check. The "both revoked, drop the key" cleanup survives a kill: a marker is committed before the revoke and finished at the next status check.
- **App-op read-back.** The code reads the op with the string `android:receive_sensitive_notifications` through `AppOpsManager.unsafeCheckOpRawNoThrow`. If the name is wrong on a build, the status reads "not allowed" and a grant reports `verified=false`, trusting the exit code.
- **Listener rebind.** `requestRebind` alone does nothing while the listener is bound, so the restart helper calls `requestUnbind()` then `requestRebind()`. Untested on a device.

## What is built
- **Modules.**
  - `:privileged_access:privileged_access_domain` is pure Kotlin with all the logic and ports.
  - `_data` holds the Shizuku route, the phone-fact reader, preferences and the Hilt module.
  - `_selfadb` holds the Self-ADB route.
  - `_presentation` holds the ViewModel and has no Compose code.
- **Commands as typed values.**
  - Four commands: grant and revoke for sensitive notifications and for secure settings. No other text can reach a command line.
  - Revoking the app-op uses `appops set ... default`, not `appops reset`, which would also wipe Farhan's usage-access op.
  - `AppId` and `ShellCommand` accept only letters, digits, `.` and `_`.
  - The Shizuku service re-checks the same allowlist (`appops` or `pm` only) on its side.
- **Status.** A passive refresh produces a `StateFlow<PrivilegedStatus>` carrying the link (`None` or `Connected(route)`) and an access state per command. It runs no command and opens no connection.
  - **Access states.**
    - Sensitive notifications: `ALLOWED`, `NOT_ALLOWED`, or `NOT_APPLICABLE` below Android 15.
    - Secure settings: `ALLOWED` or `NOT_ALLOWED`.
    - `needsSetup(access)` is derived: not allowed and no route can run the command.
  - **Observable facts.** AppOps mode and `PackageManager.checkPermission`. The `Settings.Secure` write test (writing the daltonizer switch back to its current value) runs only right after a grant, never from a status check. `appops get` was not added as a shell read-back.
  - **Foreground re-check.** The app re-checks when it returns to the foreground, through activity lifecycle callbacks in `ForegroundRecheck`.
- **Route preference.** `ASK` (default), `SELF_ADB` or `SHIZUKU`, with a pure chooser. The order is: the route named for this call, then a fixed preference, then the retained link, then ask. With a retained link a second access runs with no question and no pairing.
- **Owner update (mock-up v5).**
  - The pairing code is single use, never stored, and its `toString` prints stars.
  - Farhan keeps the adb key in `noBackupFilesDir`, with a 10-year certificate.
  - Revoke runs over the retained link.
  - Revoking both accesses deletes the adb key.
  - Typed failures: `LinkLost(NOT_PAIRED | KEY_REJECTED | WIRELESS_DEBUGGING_OFF)` and `ShizukuNotRunning`, plus route-blocked, command-failed-with-output, not-effective, busy and invalid-app-id.
  - **Access states are not cleared on a lost link.** I deviated from "clear the link and both access states": the states come from the phone, so a grant that took effect still shows `ALLOWED` while `link` is `None` and `canRevoke` is false. Clearing them would be a false statement. I can make them literal if you want that.
  - **Wireless debugging off versus key rejected.** Wireless debugging off clears the link but keeps the key. A rejected key deletes it, after one retry with a fresh port in case the port changed between discovery and connect.
- **Rebind and the red note.**
  - After a successful app-op grant, `NotificationService.requestRestart()` runs.
  - `OTP_REDACTION_SEEN` is cleared on a successful grant and when a code arrives in plain text (in `NotificationService`).
  - The Settings red note and its manual command are untouched.
- **Grayscale.** `GrayscaleViewModel.grantSecureSettings(route?)` calls the connector and puts the result in `GrayscaleState.secureSettingsGrant`. The root button and the existing guidance stay.
- **Grayscale reset before revoke.** Revoking secure settings first turns Grayscale off (`GrayscaleUtil.setGrayscaleState(false)`) while the permission is still held, otherwise the screen could stay gray with nothing able to undo it.
- **Settings backup (`SettingsCatalog`).**
  - Included: `privileged_access_route` (STRING).
  - Excluded as INTERNAL: `privileged_access_link_drop_pending`.
  - Also excluded as INTERNAL: `notification_experiment_otp_redaction_seen`. It is existing and out of scope, but exporting it would show a false red note on another phone.

## Decisions to know about
1. **The self-ADB code in `settings_rescue` could not be called.** It is an application module with `internal` classes, built to stay isolated from main-app modules. Its fixed wire client (`AdbWire`, `ConscryptTls`) is also uncommitted in the main checkout and absent from this base (there is no `AdbWire` or `ConscryptTls` at `cbc5fd5`). I copied the two wire files, with their 9-test fake-adbd test, into the new module, and wrote a new persistent key store. They are marked "adapted from settings_rescue". The clean fix is one shared `:adb_client` library for both apps once the rescue work lands.
2. **Shizuku API 13.1.5, the latest release.** I confirmed it on Maven Central's maven-metadata (latest and release both 13.1.5, last updated 2023-09-21) and downloaded the AAR. In that AAR `Shizuku.newProcess` is private (access flags 0xa), so commands run through a user service (AIDL `IExecService`, `ExecUserService`). The jar exposes `bindUserService`, `requestPermission`, `checkSelfPermission`, `shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale` and `isPreV11`, all of which I use.
3. **`minSdk` clash.** Shizuku's API library declares `minSdk` 24 and the app is 23, so I added `tools:overrideLibrary` in the app manifest. Below Android 7 the route reports "too old" and the Shizuku provider is disabled through a `values/bools.xml` resource.
4. **Shizuku's grant cannot be dropped from inside the app.** Only Shizuku's manager can change it. After both accesses are revoked, the retained Shizuku permission stays, and the UI has to say so.
5. **libadb pairing has no read timeout.** It runs on its own thread and is abandoned after 25 seconds. A stuck thread lingers until its socket fails. The rescue helper kills a whole process instead; this does not.
6. **New dependencies.** libadb-android 3.1.1 (jitpack, LGPL spake2 underneath), conscrypt-android 2.5.3 and bcpkix 1.81, plus Shizuku `api` and `provider` 13.1.5. The notices are in `privileged_access_selfadb/NOTICE.md`; the app's own licence listing is not updated.
7. **Settings red note.** It still does not appear while the app runs, which is emulator defect N1 (`otpRedactionSeen` is read once in `refreshAutomation()`). I did not touch that UI code.

## Tests
Run on Boat `bx_bngcafgz`, 0 failures in every module:

|---|---|
| `privileged_access_domain` | 57 |
| `privileged_access_data` | 5 |

| `settings_portability` | 62 |
| `settings_rescue` | 56 |
| `notification_filter_data` | 119 |
| `screen_grayscale_presentation` | 1 |
| `app` | 13 |

`:app:assembleProfileable` also passed (37 MB APK), and the merged manifest has `INTERNET` and the Shizuku provider.

- **Scenarios you asked for.** Grant A then B without pairing, revoke A keeps the link, revoke both drops the link, key rejected drops the link and returns `LinkLost(KEY_REJECTED)`.
- **Also covered.** Exact argument lists, a refresh that runs no shell, route choice and failure mapping, an interrupted revoke, the busy guard, the sentinel parser for the Self-ADB `exec:` stream, and the key file.
- **Not unit-tested.** `AndroidPhoneFacts`, `AdbDiscovery`, `AndroidSelfAdbRoute`, the Shizuku route and `GrayscaleViewModel.grantSecureSettings` — they need a device or Android classes.

## UI hooks for the next task
- `PrivilegedAccessViewModel` (Hilt) exposes `state: StateFlow<PrivilegedAccessState>` with `status`, `routePreference`, `working`, `lastResult`, `lastPairing` and `lastShizukuPermission`.
- It has these calls:
  - `status()` and `onForeground()`.
  - `grantSensitiveNotifications(route?)`, `grantSecureSettings(route?)`, `revokeSensitiveNotifications(route?)` and `revokeSecureSettings(route?)`.
  - `pairSelfAdb(code: String, pairingPort: String = "")` — a blank port means discover it.
  - `requestShizukuPermission()`, `setRoutePreference(p)`, `forgetSelfAdbKey()` and `dismissResult()`.
- Handle the `AccessResult.ChooseRoute(options)` result by showing the route picker, then call again with `route`.
- Pairing only works while the user has "Pair device with pairing code" open in Developer options, so the pairing screen has to be visible alongside it (the rescue helper had the same problem and used a freeform window).

The pairing code disappears if you switch apps."), a button to open Developer options / Wireless debugging in system settings (Settings.ACTION_APPLICATION_DEVELOPMENT_SETTINGS), pairing code field (6 digits) and port field (blank = Farhan finds it; label it optional), button "Pair and allow" (busy state "Allowing…"). content.text:
The crash is fixed in the worktree, but not yet compiled or run on a device.

**Cause.** `HomeWatcher.startWatch()` registered its receiver with no export flag. Android 14 and later throw a `SecurityException` for that, and your Android 17 build did. It's old code from the legacy launcher screen. The new Launcher tab triggers it as soon as you open the tab.

**Fix** (`core/.../util/HomeWatcher.kt`):
- It registers with `RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED`, and the call is wrapped so a failure is logged instead of crashing.
- A registered flag stops a double registration, which was the leak I'd noted earlier, and stops unregistering a receiver that was never registered.

**Not verified:**
- **Compile:** the UI agent is mid-build on Boat. Running Gradle alongside it risks the daemon out-of-memory crash, so I'll confirm the compile in the same build.
- **Device:** I haven't run it on a device, and I don't know whether Android 17 still sends the home-key broadcast to apps at all. The tab will no longer crash. The "home key resets the launcher" behaviour is untested.
- **Other tabs:** I found no other `registerReceiver` calls in the main code that lack a flag. I checked by search, not on a device.

**Progress on the rest:**
- **Connector core:** it merged cleanly. You chose to ship `INTERNET` and change the copy, so the UI agent is also rewording `SPEC.md` and the English onboarding page 1.
- **UI agent:** it is building the Special access screens to the v5 mock-up and will report when done.
The whole launcher tab idea, is it even worth it? There are a million minimal focused launchers out there and not a single one of them even comes close to fulfilling my needs...

Not as a tab. I'd keep the code but stop treating the Launcher tab as a feature.

- **A launcher is only worth having as your home screen.** Inside a tab it's just an app list, which is a worse version of your system launcher. It's also what crashed you today. Nothing exercised that code path, and the old launcher was already hidden from the main navigation in the spec.
- **Farhan's real value doesn't depend on it.** The Inbox, Summary, scroll blocker, grayscale, and time limit and mindful launch all work without it. I haven't confirmed that mindful launch (delayed launch) is independent of the launcher screen, so check that before removing anything.
- **You said none of the minimal launchers meet your needs, but I don't know what those needs are.** If one of them is something only Farhan could do as your home screen (for example, gating every app launch with its own rules), that's a different product decision. That would mean a real launcher design, not an optional tab. Tell me what's missing and I'll say whether it's worth building.

My recommendation for this APK:
- Turn the Launcher tab off by default. The feature switch in Settings › Features already hides it, so it's a one-line default change.
- Keep the code and the crash fix, and put no more work into it.
- Remove it entirely only if you're sure you'll never want Farhan as a home screen. That's a bigger and less reversible cut, so I wouldn't do it now.

Should I flip the default to off in this build?
default off and remove from builds until further notice.

- **Note under the group:** a third text for Shizuku (it cannot drop its own grant), and a variant without "both" on Android before 15, where only one switch exists. On that case the toast is "Off. Pairing forgotten."
- **Developer options button:** labelled "Open Developer options", since the intent opens that page.
- **Flow page:** the footer differs for Shizuku. Shizuku status can also read "not installed" or "too old". The title and Allowed boxes use a bold title.
- **Flow button:** "Pair and allow" stays disabled until the code is 6 digits and the port is blank or in range.
- **Done button:** uses an ink fill, not the theme accent.
- **Switched on with no link:** an access that is already allowed but has no link shows a switch that cannot revoke. Switching it off opens the flow with "not connected" shown, and the user pairs, then switches it off.
- **Red note:** hidden when sensitive notifications are allowed or not applicable (before Android 15). It no longer depends on the "hidden" flag alone.

  - `SpecialAccessFlow.kt` is the flow page.
  - `SpecialAccessController.kt` holds the hoisted flow state and turns results into snackbars or flow opens.
  - `SpecialAccessChecks.kt` and `SpecialAccessText.kt` are the system-access reads and string mapping.
- **`SettingsScreen.kt`:**
  - Owns the controller and opens the flow page on the More tab.
  - Back closes the flow and returns to More.
  - Runs a 3 s status refresh on the Notifications and More tabs, which is the fix for the note's refresh gap.
- **`SettingsComponents.kt` (core-ui):** added `SettingValueRow` and `StatusPill`.

content.text:
The new APK is sent to `pixel-9a` by Taildrop. The command exited 0, but I haven't confirmed delivery, and the last send gave a "not replying" warning. It's `research/apk/farhan-cbc5fd5-connector-v4-profileable.apk`, with the same app id (`ly.com.tahaben.farhan_alpha`) and version code 11, so it should install over your current app as before. I read both from the APK itself. The unit tests and the profileable build pass on Boat, and a check on the emulator passed all nine items.

**Check these on your phone first:**
- **Self-ADB and Shizuku have never run on a real phone.** The emulator accepts any connection, so pairing there only proved the failure messages and that the app doesn't crash. Whether the grant actually works on Android 15–17 is untested, and so is whether switching an access off kills Farhan's process.
- **Android 17 and the Launcher:** the crash you pasted came from the Launcher tab. The tab is removed from the build, and the `HomeWatcher` fix itself is only tested on the emulator's API 35, not Android 17. I don't know whether Android 17 still sends the home-key broadcast at all.
- **The app now holds the `INTERNET` permission.** I confirmed it in the APK. You chose to ship it with changed copy. The English text in `SPEC.md`, onboarding page 1 and the store listing is updated.
- **Out-of-date translations:** Arabic, Spanish, Polish and Tamil onboarding still say there is no internet permission, and so does the Arabic store listing. I did not machine-translate them. I did not check the privacy policy.
- **One ANR in the emulator**, about 50 seconds after a cold boot at roughly 91% CPU. It didn't repeat on later starts, so I think it was boot contention. It is on the emulator, not measured on your phone.

**Changes from the signed-off mock-up:**
- **Flow page:** the button reads "Open Developer options", and the port field is "Port (optional)", because the core can find the port.
- **Red note:** it keeps a manual adb line under the Allow button.
- **Access granted outside Farhan:** if an access was granted outside Farhan and there's no link, the other row stays an Allow button instead of becoming a switch.
- **Shizuku:** Farhan can't drop Shizuku's own grant, so after revoking both, the screen says so.
- **Accessibility row:** it shows "Not allowed" when off, which the mock-up never does.
- **Known leftovers:** the "Hold Up!" dialog still appears on every visit to Settings › Notifications.

**What's in it, beyond what you've already seen:**
- **Special access:** it sits under Settings › More. After the first Allow, the other access is a plain switch, and the red note's Allow runs directly once a link exists.
- **Grayscale guidance:** it now points at Special access.
- **Verification-code note:** it appears in the running Settings page within 3 seconds of Android hiding a code. It no longer waits for a restart. The core's read-back name for the app-op was also correct on the emulator's Android 15 image.

Nothing is committed. Screenshots are in `research/screens/v6/`, and the state is saved in `research/notification-ui-state.md`. The Boat sandbox runs to its TTL, about 2 hours from 02:20 MST.
